subject: Performance SLO + customer load test coordination
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jake Turner <jake.turner@finwise.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com, aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sat, 8 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + next steps on performance SLOs / load test

Hi Jake —

Great to meet yesterday. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before the load test: 

- Target SLOs you called out: p95 latency <= 200ms (inference-only), sustained throughput ~800 RPS, concurrent open streams ~200 for streaming responses.
- Streaming behavior: partial tokens should arrive within 100ms of generation, and we should preserve order for chunked outputs.
- Success criteria: p95 and p99 within targets for 90% of test windows; no more than 1% error rate; tail latency for streaming under 500ms for final chunks.

Proposed next steps:
1) You share the Locust/k6 script you plan to run (or we can use our k6 template).
2) We provide temporary test API keys + IP allowlist entries.
3) Agree on ramp schedule and test window (we suggested Aug 12 02:00-05:00 UTC).

I’ve CC’d Rishi and Aditya from solutions/infra to help with the test account, streaming behavior, and to review the script. I’ll attach our k6 starter and a CSV of test accounts so you can drop that into your runner.

Attachments: test-accounts.csv (stub), ip-allowlist.txt (stub)

Thanks — talk soon.
—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Jake Turner <jake.turner@finwise.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: FinWise Ops <ops@finwise.com>
Date: Sat, 8 Aug 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps on performance SLOs / load test

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap. Confirming the SLOs on our side: p95 <=200ms inference, p99 ideally <400ms but tolerable up to 500ms during ramp. Throughput target 800 RPS sustained for 1 hour, concurrency ~200. We will be testing streaming for a subset of calls (~20% of traffic).

A few questions:
- Can you confirm whether the streaming latency targets are measured from request time or token generation time?
- For IP allowlisting, we’ll need the exact CIDR ranges your infrastructure will use.
- For test accounts: do the test keys have reduced rate limits that could impact the test?

We’ll attach our Locust script once we clean up a couple of parameterized pieces. Tentatively agree to the Aug 12 window but would like to firm the ramp plan.

Jake Turner
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer, FinWise

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jake Turner <jake.turner@finwise.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com, aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps on performance SLOs / load test

Jake —

Answers inline and some operational details: 

- Streaming latency: we measure from request start to first token (for initial partials) and token generation time internally; for your success criteria use request->first-token latency. We'll provide both metrics in the dashboard.
- IP allowlist: please see the attached ip-allowlist.txt — those are the egress IPs we’ll use for the test. If you need CIDR aggregates we can provide them; CC’ing Aditya to confirm ownership of the exact ranges.
- Test keys: test keys will be provisioned with the same concurrency semantics as prod but with a soft quota so we can trace/test safely. They will not be throttled below the expected test targets unless they hit protection thresholds (we’ll temporarily relax protections for the window).

I attached: test-accounts.csv (sample accounts + headers) and ip-allowlist.txt (stub list).

Planned test window: Aug 12, 02:00-05:00 UTC — ramp 10m -> 30% -> 5m -> 60% -> 5m -> 100% sustain for 40m, then 10m cooldown. If that works, we’ll provision keys and open support channel.

Attaching our k6 starter template as well if you’d prefer to use k6 vs Locust.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jake Turner <jake.turner@finwise.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps on performance SLOs / load test

Hi Jake —

Quick technical notes from the infra side: 
- Streaming: our runtime flushes partial tokens as they are produced; typical first-token latency is dominated by model decode time. For streaming tests please include an endpoint that returns ~8 token chunks to mimic real workloads.
- Concurrency: we recommend testing both open websocket-style streaming (long-lived connections) and short HTTP streaming to capture resource usage patterns.
- Metrics we’ll expose: p50/p90/p95/p99, token throughput, connection count, error_class (5xx/4xx/timeout), and per-route CPU/GPU utilization counters.

I attached a k6 script stub (k6_script_v1.js) that:
- simulates 80% short requests, 20% streaming requests
- supports ramp stages via environment variables

If you want, I can sync with your infra to validate the Locust script before the run.

Aditya
Aditya Rao
Site Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Jake Turner <jake.turner@finwise.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: FinWise Ops <ops@finwise.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps on performance SLOs / load test

Thanks Aditya — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups before we finalize: 
1) Ramp schedule — can you confirm the exact timings for the ramp stages you proposed? We want deterministic steps we can script in Locust.
2) CIDR blocks — our security team needs the aggregate CIDR ranges rather than per-host IPs. Can you provide those?
3) Success criteria — for the post-test report, can you include per-route breakdowns and the raw logs (or a pointer) so our SREs can reproduce anomalies?

We’ll attach our Locust file by EOD today. Once we have the keys + CIDRs we’ll schedule a short run in our staging prior to Aug 12.

Jake

Hi Jake —

Confirming what we’ll provide by EOD today: 
- CIDR aggregates for the test egress: 54.173.0.0/18, 35.191.0.0/16 (these are examples — Aditya will validate the final list).
- Provisioned test API key: test-k_FinWise_87321 (will be valid 2026-08-11T00:00:00Z to 2026-08-13T00:00:00Z).
- Ramp script example (JSON) you can plug into Locust: 10m warmup -> 5m @30% -> 5m @60% -> 40m @100% -> 10m cooldown. I’ll paste the JSON into the HubSpot ticket and share the Drive link.
- Post-test deliverables: consolidated report (p50/p90/p95/p99, error breakdown), per-route CPU/GPU time series, and a link to raw request logs for the test window.

Next steps: you send the Locust script and confirm the staging run time. We’ll review the script (Aditya) and then enable the keys + allowlist.
